title: Why Gym Memberships Are Designed for You to Quit
alts: The Gym Business Model: Why They Want You to Quit
Why Cancelling a Gym Is Harder Than Joining One
line1: Why do gyms want you to sign up and never show up? A famous study found most members would save money paying per visit instead.
summary: Dave signs a gym contract on January 1st, goes three times, and keeps paying all year. We break down why: Planet Fitness has about 7,200 members per club (way more than any floor holds), the January sign-up spike and 'Quitter's Day' drop-off, the famous DellaVigna & Malmendier study proving most monthly members would save money paying per visit, the psychology (present bias) behind why smart people still sign long contracts, the hard-to-cancel tactics (certified mail, in-person only, 30-day notice), and the FTC's 'click-to-cancel' rule that got vacated by a federal court in 2025. Then, practical ways to avoid the trap: pay-per-visit apps, month-to-month plans, and an honest 'will I actually go' test before you sign.
